records.claim_text: The overarching design principles are stated as five adjectives: role-based, adaptive, simple, coherent, delightful. These are named as guidance for every app design decision.
records.evidence_quote: the SAP Fiori design principles as the overarching guidance: Role-based, adaptive, simple, coherent, and delightful

records.claim_text: The original 2013 principle set was role-based, simple, responsive, coherent, delightful; the modern set substitutes adaptive for responsive.
records.evidence_quote: the principles of role-based, simple, responsive, coherent and delightful apps

records.claim_text: A floorplan is defined as a page-level layout assembled from patterns and components, sitting above components and below templates in the system hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: A floorplan is the UI layout consisting of patterns and components

records.claim_text: A page occupies the whole viewport and is composed of exactly three zones: a header, a content area, and an optional footer toolbar.
records.evidence_quote: A page uses the entire viewport of an app and consists of three main areas
records.behaviour_description: Every screen is a single full-viewport page. The top zone carries page-wide context and page-wide actions and stays present; the middle zone is the working surface; the bottom zone is reserved for closing/finalizing actions and only materialises when such actions exist.
records.density_notes: Three-zone split is density-independent; only the pixel heights of header rows and toolbars change between comfortable and compact settings.
records.keyboard_notes: Tab order runs header then content then footer, matching visual reading order.
records.a11y_notes: Zones should be exposed as landmark regions (banner/main/contentinfo) so screen-reader users can jump between them.

records.claim_text: One generic collapsible-header page layout is declared the foundation for all pages; specific floorplans are specialisations of it rather than separate layouts.
records.evidence_quote: The dynamic page is the foundation for all pages in SAP Fiori.
records.behaviour_description: A single skeleton control supplies the header/content/footer scaffold plus built-in responsive behaviour; floorplans fill that scaffold with prescribed element combinations. Building a bespoke page means filling the same skeleton, not inventing a new one.
records.density_notes: Skeleton inherits the app-wide density class; do not mix densities within one page.
records.keyboard_notes: Expand/collapse of the header must be reachable and operable from the keyboard.
records.a11y_notes: Collapsing the header must not remove header actions from the accessibility tree.

records.claim_text: A floorplan must be built as the page itself, never nested inside the content area of another page skeleton.
records.evidence_quote: Never insert a whole floorplan into just the content area of the dynamic page layout.
records.behaviour_description: Header elements of a floorplan bind to the page header slot and footer actions to the page footer slot. Nesting a whole floorplan inside a content area produces duplicated headers, two scroll contexts and broken sticky behaviour.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Nesting creates duplicate landmark regions and a confusing tab sequence.
records.a11y_notes: Only one banner-level header per page.

records.claim_text: An app chooses either one page at a time or a multi-column layout showing up to three related pages side by side for list-detail relationships.
records.evidence_quote: a flexible column layout for list-detail relationships (up to three pages side by side)
records.behaviour_description: Choice is made once per app. Multi-column keeps parent context visible while the user drills into a child, so navigation feels like widening rather than replacing the view.
records.density_notes: Narrow columns force compact spacing; content inside each column must be responsive down to phone width.
records.keyboard_notes: Focus must move into the newly opened column when a list row is activated.
records.a11y_notes: Each column needs its own accessible name so users can tell which pane has focus.
maps_to_screens: SO List + SO Detail + Line Item Detail

records.claim_text: Floorplans are grouped by intent: overview of information and tasks; listing several objects; managing one object; navigating to a single object.
records.evidence_quote: List several objects: list report, analytical list report, worklist
records.behaviour_description: Floorplan selection is driven by user intent, not by data volume. Overview answers what needs attention; list floorplans answer which items; object floorplans answer what about this item.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: The overview floorplan exists so one role can see, filter and react to information drawn from several applications on a single page.
records.evidence_quote: Provide an overview of information and tasks: overview page
records.behaviour_description: A filter bar at the top applies globally to every content container below it, so changing one filter re-scopes the whole page at once.
records.density_notes: Card grid reflows by breakpoint; card interiors keep app density.
records.keyboard_notes: Tab order runs filter bar then cards in visual order.
records.a11y_notes: Each card needs an accessible name matching its visible title.

records.claim_text: Every floorplan except the guided-process wizard and the single-input initial page can be generated declaratively by the metadata-driven UI framework.
records.evidence_quote: Except for the wizard and initial page, all floorplans are available as SAP Fiori elements.

records.claim_text: A single universal header sits above every screen and carries both product-global functions and product-context elements.
records.evidence_quote: The shell bar is a universal header at the top of all screens.
records.behaviour_description: Left cluster: navigation affordance, optional back, branding/product name that returns to home. Centre-right: a context area for product-wide elements. Right cluster: search, assistant, notifications bell, extra actions, help, profile menu, product switcher.
records.density_notes: Shell height is fixed and independent of the app content density beneath it.
records.keyboard_notes: Shell is the first tab stop of the document, before app content.
records.a11y_notes: Expose as a banner landmark; every icon-only control needs a text label.

records.claim_text: The user profile entry point is mandatory in the shell header and is the gateway to the user menu.
records.evidence_quote: Profile (mandatory): Provides access to the user menu.
records.behaviour_description: Profile avatar opens a menu holding identity, settings, theme/appearance and sign-out. Shell actions must not be duplicated inside this menu.
records.density_notes: Menu items follow the shell density, not the app density.
records.keyboard_notes: Menu opens on Enter/Space and closes on Escape, restoring focus to the avatar.
records.a11y_notes: Avatar button needs an accessible name identifying the signed-in user.

records.claim_text: Under width pressure the shell degrades in a fixed order, collapsing the search field first so all other elements stay visible longest.
records.evidence_quote: The search field collapses first to ensure that all other content remains visible.
records.behaviour_description: Degradation sequence: search collapses to an icon, then extra actions move to an overflow menu, then context elements drop by declared priority, then the product name hides, and finally search itself moves into the overflow.
records.density_notes: Breakpoint-driven, independent of comfortable/compact.
records.keyboard_notes: Items moved to overflow must remain reachable through the overflow button.
records.a11y_notes: Badge counts on overflowed actions must surface on the overflow trigger.

records.claim_text: A shell-level back button is discouraged; browser history is the preferred back mechanism, and any shell back control hides when no history exists.
records.evidence_quote: Avoid using a Back button in the shell bar; use the browser's Back button instead.
records.behaviour_description: Implies app routes must be real URLs with proper history entries. Deep-linked entry shows no back affordance because there is nothing to return to.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: A hidden back button is preferable to a disabled one.

records.claim_text: The launchpad is a persistent shell giving role-based access to apps, with the shell header always visible above whatever app is running.
records.evidence_quote: a shell that provides a role-based access to SAP Fiori apps
records.behaviour_description: Apps are embedded inside the shell and cannot alter it. The shell owns logo, navigation, enterprise search, notifications and personalisation; apps own only the page below.
records.density_notes: Shell and app can carry different densities; the shell enforces its own.
records.keyboard_notes: Focus must not be trapped inside an embedded app.
records.a11y_notes: Shell and app content need distinct landmark roles.

records.claim_text: Home navigation is organised as spaces per business role, each space holding one or more pages, each page holding titled sections of tiles.
records.evidence_quote: A space serves as an entry point for a business role
records.behaviour_description: Spaces appear as top-level navigation items; selecting one reveals its pages. Space titles name a work area rather than the role itself; page titles are task-oriented and never repeat the space title.
records.density_notes: Tile grid reflows by breakpoint.
records.keyboard_notes: Top-level navigation is a tab-like list traversable with arrow keys.
records.a11y_notes: Section headings should be real headings so the page outline is navigable.

records.claim_text: Home pages should stay lean, with a recommended two to five sections per page, optionally including a quick-access and an insights section.
records.evidence_quote: we recommend using between 2 and 5 sections per page
records.behaviour_description: Sections group tiles semantically. Reusing the same two section names across spaces gives users a stable mental map when switching roles.
records.density_notes: Section titles are optional; omitting them tightens vertical rhythm.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: The list report floorplan lets users view and act on a large item set, and typically serves as the entry point into an object detail page.
records.evidence_quote: With a list report, users can view and work with a large set of items.
records.behaviour_description: Filter-first pattern: a collapsible filter region on top, a result region below. Use it when the user knows roughly what they want but not which record; not when they already know the exact record.
records.density_notes: Compact density is the norm on desktop because row count per screen is the primary value.
records.keyboard_notes: Filter fields, then Go, then table; row activation opens the detail.
records.a11y_notes: Result count changes must be announced when filters are applied.

records.claim_text: The list report splits into a header area holding title/variant plus the filter bar, and a content area holding the table or chart with its own toolbar.
records.evidence_quote: divided into a header area and a content area
records.behaviour_description: Header title row carries the page title or saved view plus global non-finalizing actions. Header content carries the filter bar. Content area carries an optional view switcher, one toolbar per view, and one or more tables/charts. Footer appears only for finalizing actions and the message indicator.
records.density_notes: Two toolbar levels exist: page-level in the header, content-level above the table. Do not merge them.
records.keyboard_notes: Content toolbar is reachable directly after the filter region.
records.a11y_notes: Table needs a caption or accessible name derived from the view title.

records.claim_text: Live filtering that refreshes results on every change is the recommended default; a manual Go-button mode is reserved for cases with load performance problems.
records.evidence_quote: The live update mode (recommended) triggers filtering immediately whenever a filter setting is changed.
records.behaviour_description: In manual mode the result region must be visibly stale-marked and busy until Go is pressed, so the filter description and the visible rows never silently disagree.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: In manual mode initial focus goes to the Go button; in live mode to the first filter field.
records.a11y_notes: Live filtering must announce the new result count without stealing focus.

records.claim_text: The filter region collapses automatically as the user scrolls into results and re-expands on scrolling back; users can pin it open.
records.evidence_quote: The header content collapses when the user scrolls down the page
records.behaviour_description: Auto-collapse is disabled when the content area owns its own scrollbar (desktop grid/tree/analytical tables); in that case an explicit show/hide filters control replaces it. When collapsed, a summary line states how many filters are active and names up to five of them.
records.density_notes: Collapsing reclaims significant vertical space, which matters most in compact density on short viewports.
records.keyboard_notes: Expand/collapse and pin must both be keyboard-operable controls.
records.a11y_notes: Collapse must not remove the filter summary from the accessible name of the region.

records.claim_text: Initial focus is conditional: first filter field or Go when the filter region is open, first empty mandatory filter if any, otherwise the first result row.
records.evidence_quote: If the header is collapsed, set the focus on the first table row.
records.behaviour_description: Focus lands where the user's next action is, so keyboard users skip zero tab stops on page entry.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: This is the core keyboard-efficiency rule for list screens; replicate it per floorplan.
records.a11y_notes: Programmatic focus on load must not scroll the page unexpectedly.

records.claim_text: A single page-level saved-view control should govern filters, selected tab, and all table and chart settings together, rather than one control per component.
records.evidence_quote: we recommend using one variant management control for the whole page
records.behaviour_description: Users pick a default view applied at app start; an optional setting controls whether selecting a view runs it immediately or lets the user adjust filters first (only meaningful in manual mode).
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: View name acts as a menu button opening the view dialogs.
records.a11y_notes: Unsaved-change marker must also be conveyed non-visually.

records.claim_text: When no filters are set the collapsed header shows an explicit no-filters-active statement rather than an empty area.
records.evidence_quote: If no filters have been applied, the summary text is: No filters active
records.behaviour_description: The summary always states filter state explicitly, so a user scrolled deep into results never has to guess whether the result set is scoped.
records.density_notes: Single line; truncate with an ellipsis beyond five named filters.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Summary should be part of the region's accessible description.

records.claim_text: The expanded filter bar comprises optional saved views, an optional basic search, filter inputs with labels above, an optional Go button, and an adapt-filters entry.
records.evidence_quote: lets users set criteria to limit the data loaded and displayed in a table
records.floorplan: List Report / Overview Page / Analytical List Page
records.behaviour_description: Filter inputs sit in a horizontal linear flow that wraps to new lines as width shrinks; all inputs adopt the width of the widest one for visual cohesion. Only a subset of available filters is shown by default; the rest live behind an adapt dialog.
records.density_notes: Labels sit above fields, which costs vertical space but survives localisation and keeps wrapping predictable.
records.keyboard_notes: Mandatory filters are marked with an asterisk next to the label.
records.a11y_notes: Asterisk alone is insufficient; required state must be programmatic.

records.claim_text: The adapt-filters entry point shows the count of active filters in parentheses, and a filter can be active while not visible in the bar.
records.evidence_quote: the number of active filters is displayed in parentheses
records.behaviour_description: This is the safety valve for hidden scoping: a user can always see that filters exist beyond the visible fields, and reach them in one click.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Count must be in the button's accessible name, not only visually.

records.claim_text: Saved views persist filter settings plus control parameters such as sort order, grouping, column visibility and table layout; the UI label is view, not variant.
records.evidence_quote: Variants store view settings, such as filter settings or control parameters.
records.behaviour_description: Three dialogs support the pattern: pick a view, manage views (default, favourites, delete), save a new view. Vendor-shipped standard views are permanent favourites and cannot be edited or deleted.
records.density_notes: On phones all three dialogs open full screen.
records.keyboard_notes: The view name is the single entry point to all three dialogs.
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: When the user changes settings away from the loaded view, the view name is marked with an asterisk to signal unsaved changes.
records.evidence_quote: the view is marked with an asterisk (*) to indicate the unsaved changes
records.behaviour_description: Adding or removing a filter field counts as a change, not only changing values, so structural personalisation is also tracked.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Dirty state must be exposed textually as well as by the asterisk glyph.

records.claim_text: The object page displays and categorises all relevant information for one object, supporting display, edit and create modes on the same structure.
records.evidence_quote: used to display and categorize all relevant information about an object
records.behaviour_description: Three mandatory-or-optional parts: a collapsible header carrying identity and context, an optional navigation bar, and a sectioned content area. Layout stays identical across display, edit and create so nothing moves when the mode changes.
records.density_notes: Compact on desktop; the header is the main density lever because it is the tallest fixed element.
records.keyboard_notes: In edit mode focus goes to the first empty mandatory field, else the first editable element or action.
records.a11y_notes: Section titles must be real headings to give a navigable outline.

records.claim_text: Header context is built from typed facet containers arranged inline with left float, wrapping to the next line when they do not fit.
records.evidence_quote: There are several types of header facets for different kinds of data.
records.behaviour_description: Facet kinds cover label-value groups, free text, an image, a large key figure, a micro chart, a progress bar and a rating. Each facet sizes to its content without truncating. At most one image facet, pinned left, which shrinks and moves beside the title when the header collapses.
records.density_notes: Keep facets few; a tall header pushes the working content below the fold. Omitting the image is the biggest single height saving.
records.keyboard_notes: Facets with press events must be focusable buttons or links.
records.a11y_notes: Invisible or icon-only labels in a label-value facet still require text alternatives.

records.claim_text: Header context disappears either by scrolling the page down or by activating an explicit collapse indicator; the title row remains.
records.evidence_quote: The header content is hidden by scrolling down the page or clicking the collapse indicator.
records.behaviour_description: Because the header snaps away on scroll, it cannot host editable form fields; editable header data is relocated into a temporary first section in global edit mode, or edited via a dedicated dialog or subpage in partial edit mode.
records.density_notes: Collapse is the primary vertical-space recovery mechanism on detail screens.
records.keyboard_notes: Collapse indicator is a discrete focusable toggle.
records.a11y_notes: Global actions must remain enabled and reachable while collapsed.

records.claim_text: Anchor navigation is the default: a horizontal strip of links that scrolls the single long page to a section while remaining visible.
records.evidence_quote: The anchor bar is the default navigation control for the object page.
records.behaviour_description: Anchors mirror sections and subsections. Excess anchors move into an overflow menu opening a hierarchical list; as the user scrolls, the strip scrolls horizontally to keep the active anchor visible. Activating an anchor scrolls to the section content, not to its title.
records.density_notes: In compact density the horizontal overflow arrow appears only on hover; in comfortable density it is always visible.
records.keyboard_notes: Left and right arrow keys move between anchor links.
records.a11y_notes: Active anchor state must be programmatically exposed, not colour-only.

records.claim_text: Activating an anchor or an overflow entry scrolls to the section content rather than to the section title.
records.evidence_quote: Move between anchor links.
records.behaviour_description: Scrolling to content rather than the heading avoids wasting the top of the viewport on a heading the user just read in the anchor strip.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Arrow keys traverse anchors; Enter activates.
records.a11y_notes: Programmatic focus should follow the scroll so screen readers land in the target section.

records.claim_text: Tab navigation is the alternative to anchors and is chosen when each topic on the page carries heavy content such as long tables or lists.
records.evidence_quote: Use tab bar navigation if your page covers different topics that each have complex content
records.behaviour_description: Sections become tabs and subsections become the tab's internal content, so the same content model serves both navigation modes and can be switched by configuration. Tabs are text-only with an optional item counter in parentheses; a dropdown arrow can expose subsection anchors within a tab.
records.density_notes: Tabs shorten the page and cap the amount of DOM rendered at once, which is the performance argument for complex objects.
records.keyboard_notes: Tab labels should be title case, not upper case.
records.a11y_notes: Use proper tab semantics with selected state; each panel labelled by its tab.

records.claim_text: On small screens anchor navigation degrades to a dropdown list showing the current section, while tab navigation instead uses a horizontal carousel overflow.
records.evidence_quote: On small screens, the anchor bar becomes a dropdown list.
records.behaviour_description: The two navigation modes deliberately degrade differently, so the small-screen experience is a genuine design choice and not an automatic consequence of picking anchors or tabs.
records.density_notes: Dropdown consumes one row regardless of section count; carousel keeps direct access at the cost of horizontal swiping.
records.keyboard_notes: Dropdown must be operable with arrow keys and Escape.
records.a11y_notes: Current section must be the dropdown's displayed and announced value.

records.claim_text: Sections are pure containers that may hold only subsections; actual content and local action toolbars live at subsection level.
records.evidence_quote: Sections can only contain subsections, not content.
records.behaviour_description: The first section carries no title. If a section has exactly one subsection, the subsection title is promoted to name the section and no submenu appears. Where a subsection contains a single table or chart with the same name, the redundant inner title is suppressed.
records.density_notes: Suppressing duplicate titles and reducing vertical space in single-table subsections is an explicit density lever.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Heading levels must stay consistent when titles are suppressed.

records.claim_text: Subsections support progressive disclosure: the app chooses what shows initially and the user can always reveal everything via a show-more toggle.
records.evidence_quote: Subsections have a progressive disclosure mechanism to show and hide content.
records.behaviour_description: The toggle sits bottom-right of the subsection. Hidden items are not rendered until revealed, so disclosure is also a load-cost control, not only a visual one.
records.density_notes: Primary tool for keeping detail pages scannable while still holding the full record.
records.keyboard_notes: Toggle is a normal focusable button with an expanded/collapsed state.
records.a11y_notes: Expanded state must be programmatically exposed.

records.claim_text: Form fields use top-aligned labels, which reduce completion time and behave better with long labels and localisation.
records.evidence_quote: Use top-aligned labels for form fields.
records.behaviour_description: Forms live inside subsections, one form per subsection, each form group occupying a column. The subsection title serves as the form title, and actions are placed either at subsection or group level but not both.
records.density_notes: Top labels cost vertical space but stabilise horizontal rhythm; they are the trade chosen for multi-language ERP forms.
records.keyboard_notes: Label-field association must be explicit for every field.
records.a11y_notes: Never rely on placeholder text as the label.

records.claim_text: The generated-UI framework defaults to a reduced column count for forms and offers an extended-column option to raise information density at each breakpoint.
records.evidence_quote: SAP Fiori elements, by default, provide reduced content density for form content

records.claim_text: Anchor-navigated detail pages should carry at most four desktop grid tables to avoid cognitive overload; more tables require tabs or navigation away.
records.evidence_quote: use no more than 4 grid tables to prevent cognitive overload
records.behaviour_description: Row-count thresholds drive the pattern: show immediately up to roughly twenty rows, lazy-load with a more control up to around a hundred, switch to tab navigation between roughly fifty and two hundred, and navigate to a dedicated page beyond that with a right-aligned show-all link carrying the total count.
records.density_notes: Embedded grid tables need at least four visible rows and must avoid a second nested scrollbar wherever possible.
records.keyboard_notes: A nested scroll region creates a keyboard trap risk; prefer navigation for large sets.
records.a11y_notes: Show-all link text must include the entity and total count.

records.claim_text: Detail pages load progressively section by section as the user scrolls, showing content before the whole page is ready.
records.evidence_quote: the object page loads section by section to show users some content
records.behaviour_description: Content hidden behind a show-more toggle is not fetched or rendered until revealed. Slow sections show a busy indicator over that section only, and a skeleton placeholder is used for the initial render.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Focus must not jump when a lower section finishes loading.
records.a11y_notes: Busy state must be announced for the affected region, not the whole page.

records.claim_text: Breadcrumbs sit above the object title and are limited to drilldown levels within the object hierarchy, not cross-app or cross-floorplan links.
records.evidence_quote: A breadcrumb is displayed above the object title.
records.behaviour_description: Breadcrumbs are paired with paging arrows in the layout-action area so a user can step to the previous or next sibling record without returning to the list.
records.density_notes: One extra row above the title; omit for single-level objects.
records.keyboard_notes: Paging arrows must be reachable and never move into overflow.
records.a11y_notes: Expose as a navigation landmark with an accessible name.

records.claim_text: A breadcrumb is secondary navigation showing a page's position in the application hierarchy, used for drilldown and not for cross-application jumps.
records.evidence_quote: A breadcrumb (or breadcrumb trail) is a type of secondary navigation
records.behaviour_description: Two variants exist: a standard trail whose final item is plain text for the current page, and a detail-page variant that omits the current page entirely so every item is a link.
records.density_notes: Single row; never wraps to a second line.
records.keyboard_notes: Items are links in hierarchical order.
records.a11y_notes: Current page should be marked as current when present.

records.claim_text: Under width pressure breadcrumb links collapse into a dropdown starting from the point of origin; the final element never collapses and truncates instead.
records.evidence_quote: The last element in the breadcrumb is always visible, and should never collapse
records.behaviour_description: On desktop and tablet the dropdown lists only the hidden links; on phones it lists the whole trail in hierarchical order so the collapsed control becomes a complete navigator.
records.density_notes: Horizontal layout is invariant; links always sit side by side.
records.keyboard_notes: Dropdown opens with Enter and closes with Escape.
records.a11y_notes: Hidden items must remain reachable via the dropdown, never dropped from the DOM.

records.claim_text: The analytical list page combines stepwise analysis, drilldown root-cause investigation and transactional action on a single page.
records.evidence_quote: The analytical list page (ALP) offers a unique way to analyze data step by step
records.behaviour_description: Distinguishing test against a plain list: if drilldown is rare, or chart and table need not interact, or the user does not need to see the effect of an action on a key figure, the simpler list floorplan suffices.
records.density_notes: Chart plus table on one page is inherently dense; charts must remain legible at compact spacing.
records.keyboard_notes: Chart selections must be reachable without a pointer.
records.a11y_notes: Chart-encoded filter values need textual equivalents.

records.claim_text: The expanded header offers a switch between a chart-based visual filter bar and a conventional field-based filter bar.
records.evidence_quote: switch between the visual filter bar and the filter bar using the filter type switch
records.behaviour_description: Visual filters render each filter as a small chart enriched by a measure, so choosing a filter value and seeing its magnitude are the same gesture.
records.density_notes: Visual filters are far taller than field filters; the collapsed header state matters more here.
records.keyboard_notes: The filter type switch is a persistent header control.
records.a11y_notes: Every visual filter needs an equivalent accessible value list.

records.claim_text: The content area toggles between a combined chart-and-table view, a chart-only view and a table-only view.
records.evidence_quote: a hybrid view (chart and table), a chart-only view, or a table-only view
records.behaviour_description: In the combined view chart and table are interdependent: selecting in the chart re-scopes the table, which is what separates this floorplan from a list report that merely offers a chart alternative.
records.density_notes: Combined view halves the vertical budget for each half; compact density is effectively mandatory.
records.keyboard_notes: View switch is a segmented control at the top of the content area.
records.a11y_notes: Selected view must be programmatically indicated.

records.claim_text: Applications may not restrict which header or content views are offered; all filter and view options are always available to the user.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot restrict the available views at app level.

records.claim_text: Key figure tiles are not responsive: pages carrying them are unsupported below desktop width and constrain use inside multi-column layouts.
records.evidence_quote: KPIs are not supported on size S.
records.behaviour_description: On phone width only chart-only or table-only views are offered, and the table-only view supports the responsive table type only; if no responsive table exists the chart view is shown with no switch at all.
records.density_notes: Key figure tiles are the single least responsive element on the floorplan.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: The worklist is a stripped-down list floorplan with no filter bar, intended for processing a predefined, comparably small set of items one by one.
records.evidence_quote: the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar
records.behaviour_description: Because there is no filter bar, a header title becomes mandatory unless page-level saved views are enabled. Search moves into the table toolbar, the table title carries the row count, and the table grows on scroll by default. Sort, filter, group and column settings are reached through a settings entry point.
records.density_notes: Removing the filter region reclaims the whole header content zone for rows.
records.keyboard_notes: Initial focus naturally lands on the first row since there is no filter region.
records.a11y_notes: Row count in the table title should be exposed as part of the table's accessible name.

records.claim_text: The worklist is selected when the item set is predefined and a filter bar is not needed; predefined views such as all or to-be-assigned are still possible.
records.evidence_quote: Process a predefined set of objects
records.behaviour_description: This is the closest documented equivalent of an approval or task inbox screen: a bounded queue the user works through, with named views instead of ad-hoc filtering.
records.density_notes: Compact rows maximise queue throughput.
records.keyboard_notes: Bulk selection and a bulk action toolbar should be keyboard reachable.
records.a11y_notes: Selection count must be announced when it changes.

records.claim_text: Each topic or task on an overview page is a card; the page is only a framework that arranges cards for one role.
records.evidence_quote: Each task or topic is represented by a card (or content container).
records.behaviour_description: Content from several source applications appears side by side without screen switching, and small in-place actions let the user respond without leaving the page.
records.density_notes: Two layouts exist: fixed card sizing and a resizable card grid where the user controls card dimensions.
records.keyboard_notes: Cards must be traversable in visual order.
records.a11y_notes: Card header acts as a link; its accessible name must state the destination.

records.claim_text: An overview page is only justified with at least three cards of mixed types drawing on two or more applications; below that a detail page is the right answer.
records.evidence_quote: You plan to have at least three cards.
records.behaviour_description: The overview is explicitly distinguished from a home page: a home page launches apps and uses tiles with no actions, whereas the overview is a role-specific street-level view using cards with micro actions.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: A card has exactly two mandatory zones, a header and a content area; a footer exists only for the quick-view card type.
records.evidence_quote: Each card comprises two components: a header area and a content area.
records.behaviour_description: The whole header is one click target navigating to the source application. The header holds a mandatory title, an optional subtitle, a counter of shown versus total items, and an overflow menu offering refresh of that card only and adding the card to a personal home area.
records.density_notes: Header height is variable and expands to fit wrapped text; titles beyond three lines truncate, subtitles beyond one line truncate.
records.keyboard_notes: Header must be a single focusable link, not a click handler on a div.
records.a11y_notes: Counter must be part of the card's accessible description.

records.claim_text: Cards are strictly read-only previews with micro actions; they never contain editable fields.
records.evidence_quote: However, cards never have editable fields.
records.behaviour_description: Editing always means navigating to the owning application. This keeps validation, draft handling and messaging in one place rather than duplicated on the overview.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: The card counter states items shown against total relevant items, and disappears entirely when all relevant items are already visible.
records.evidence_quote: Format: [Items on Card] of [Total Items] Example: 5 of 40
records.behaviour_description: The counter is right-aligned and never truncates; the title wraps instead. A scaling factor replaces exact digits above one thousand, and enlarging a resizable card restores the exact number.
records.density_notes: Counter width flexes with the data; reserve space so titles do not reflow on refresh.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Scaled counters should expose the exact value where known.

records.claim_text: A guided creation flow must have at least three and at most eight steps; fewer means the wizard adds only clicks, more means the task should be restructured.
records.evidence_quote: The flow should consist of a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 8 steps.
records.behaviour_description: The wizard is justified by task length or unfamiliarity, not by field count. For routine daily tasks a normal edit screen is preferred because the guidance becomes friction.
records.density_notes: Only one step's fields are visible at a time, so per-step density can be generous.
records.keyboard_notes: Progress indicator steps should be reachable for backward navigation.
records.a11y_notes: Current step and total step count must be announced.

records.claim_text: A wizard has two screens: a walkthrough that reveals form sections in sequence, and a read-only summary for final assessment before submission.
records.evidence_quote: The wizard has two screens: the walkthrough screen
records.behaviour_description: The step control mirrors the detail-page choice: an anchor mode where all steps live on one scrolling page with a next-step control appearing below completed content, or a tab mode where each step is a subpage with both next and previous controls in the footer. On the last step the forward control relabels to review. From the summary the user edits by returning, not by inline editing.
records.density_notes: Progress bar shows completed, current and upcoming states; keep step titles short enough to survive narrow widths.
records.keyboard_notes: In tab mode the forward action sits right of the backward action, matching the positive-path-right rule.
records.a11y_notes: Completed/current/upcoming step state must not be colour-only.

records.claim_text: A wizard may run either as a full-screen page or inside a modal dialog; the modal form is chosen when the user must return quickly to the triggering page.
records.evidence_quote: you can use the wizard both in full screen mode and in a modal dialog
records.behaviour_description: A standalone flow unrelated to its trigger belongs on a full page. Cancelling with modified fields raises a data-loss warning; long flows may offer a save-as-draft action in the footer.
records.density_notes: Modal width is flexible, which is one of the stated reasons to choose it.
records.keyboard_notes: Modal must trap focus and restore it to the trigger on close.
records.a11y_notes: Dialog needs an accessible name naming the task.

records.claim_text: The initial page reduces the entry interaction to one assisted input field that resolves directly to a single object, with no intermediate result list.
records.evidence_quote: The interaction point on the screen is a single input field
records.behaviour_description: Built on the detail-page skeleton with the title replaced by the input. Header starts collapsed, expands once an object is found, and collapses again on scroll while the input stays permanently visible so the next lookup needs no navigation. A new search that returns nothing resets to the collapsed initial state with a message in the content area.
records.density_notes: Field width should fit the longest expected identifier plus localisation headroom, never the full screen width except on phones.
records.keyboard_notes: Initial focus goes to the input so a scanned or typed code needs no click.
records.a11y_notes: Empty-state hint text should be an illustrated message with a real text alternative.

records.claim_text: The single input uses search-as-you-type assistance and escalates to a selection dialog only when one term could match several objects.
records.evidence_quote: The assisted input uses the live search feature (search-as-you-type) to speed up the search.
records.behaviour_description: Suggestion output can range from a single attribute to a full table of candidate values. When the user picks from the dialog it closes and the object renders in the content area below.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Suggestions must be arrow-key navigable and selectable with Enter.
records.a11y_notes: Suggestion list needs live-region semantics announcing result counts.

records.claim_text: The page header is split into a mandatory title bar and an optional collapsible content region beneath it.
records.evidence_quote: The dynamic page header contains the header title (mandatory) and the header content (optional).
records.behaviour_description: Title bar slots: title on the left (text, link, saved-view control or an input for the lookup floorplan); subtitle or filter summary below the title; breadcrumb above the title; key information centre-left; global actions right; layout actions furthest right. Global actions stay enabled and in place when the header collapses.
records.density_notes: Layout actions sit inline with global actions above roughly 1280 px column width, and move to a separate line below that.
records.keyboard_notes: Global actions must not be disabled or removed on collapse.
records.a11y_notes: Title should be the page's primary heading.

records.claim_text: Breadcrumbs are suppressed in multi-column mode and appear only when a single column occupies the full screen.
records.evidence_quote: in the flexible column layout, the breadcrumb is only available in full screen mode
records.behaviour_description: The columns themselves already express the hierarchy, so a breadcrumb inside a narrow column would restate visible structure and consume scarce width.
records.density_notes: Saves one header row per column.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Column relationship must then be conveyed by column accessible names.

records.claim_text: The base page control is an empty skeleton; a higher-level semantic wrapper with predefined slots is recommended for hand-built pages over assembling the skeleton manually.
records.evidence_quote: The dynamic page is a skeleton structure that comes with empty content containers

records.claim_text: The multi-column layout shows up to three pages side by side with user-resizable columns and a full-screen mode for the rightmost column.
records.evidence_quote: The flexible column layout offers different layouts with up to three columns
records.behaviour_description: It is a container only and supplies no content of its own. Any responsive floorplan can fill a column except a launchpad or an overview page, which are explicitly excluded.
records.density_notes: Each column must remain usable down to phone width because it may be rendered narrow.
records.keyboard_notes: A draggable splitter needs a keyboard-operable equivalent.
records.a11y_notes: Column boundaries should be exposed as separate regions.
maps_to_screens: SO List + SO Detail + Line Item

records.claim_text: Default two-column ratios are one third to two thirds or the reverse, with three fixed three-column ratios; users may drag the splitter to any ratio.
records.evidence_quote: 33% : 66% or 66% : 33% for 2 columns
records.behaviour_description: Three-column defaults distribute as quarter/quarter/half, quarter/half/quarter or half/quarter/quarter, giving the user a way to emphasise whichever level they are working in. The splitter hides when a column can shrink no further.
records.density_notes: A quarter-width column is close to phone width; design content for that floor.
records.keyboard_notes: Layout presets give a keyboard path to ratios that dragging alone would not.
records.a11y_notes: Splitter needs a role and value semantics if implemented.
maps_to_screens: SO List + SO Detail + Line Item

records.claim_text: At tablet width only two columns are possible and the user switches which pair is shown; at phone width the layout degrades to a single full-screen column.
records.evidence_quote: there is no multi-column layout for Size S
records.behaviour_description: Three pages can still be loaded at tablet width; the user toggles between showing columns one and two or columns two and three. On phones the rightmost column takes the whole screen and the full-screen action disappears since it is meaningless.
records.density_notes: Degradation is by breakpoint, not by density setting.
records.keyboard_notes: Close remains available on phone width in the second and third columns.
records.a11y_notes: Announce which level is displayed after a degradation switch.

records.claim_text: Close and enter/exit full screen appear only in the last visible column, always sit as the final layout actions, and never move into an overflow menu.
records.evidence_quote: the user can switch the rightmost column to full screen mode
records.behaviour_description: Their position is deliberately stable so users build muscle memory, and closing the second column while the third is minimised closes both. Full-screen and close are always rendered side by side, full-screen left of close.
records.density_notes: Reserve fixed space for these two controls so global actions do not shift when they appear.
records.keyboard_notes: Must remain reachable at all widths since they never overflow.
records.a11y_notes: Icon-only controls need persistent text labels.

records.claim_text: The multi-column layout is explicitly not a workbench or tools layout; supporting side content belongs in a dedicated side container instead.
records.evidence_quote: You want to build a workbench or tools layout.
records.behaviour_description: Columns must express a drilldown hierarchy. Using them for a main-plus-tools arrangement, a dashboard of unrelated pages, multiple instances of the same object type, or splitting one object across columns are all named anti-patterns.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: A side panel is a collapsible strip on either edge of the page giving quick access to contextual tools without leaving the page.
records.evidence_quote: positioned on the right or left side of the main page content
records.behaviour_description: A vertical icon rail holds tabs; selecting one opens its content panel directly and re-selecting closes it. With a single tool the rail collapses to just an expand control whose tooltip must match the panel title. Excess tools move into an overflow at the end of the rail.
records.density_notes: Recommended ceiling of five actions keeps the rail scannable.
records.keyboard_notes: Rail tabs and the close control must both be focusable.
records.a11y_notes: Tab tooltips must match their content area titles so labels are consistent.

records.claim_text: Opening the side panel pushes the main content sideways rather than overlaying it, and its default expanded width is 320 pixels.
records.evidence_quote: When expanded, the side panel pushes the main page content sideways.
records.behaviour_description: Push rather than overlay means the main content must remain fully usable at reduced width; the panel can also carry an optional resize handle.
records.density_notes: Main content must survive losing 320 px; plan the narrowest table column set accordingly.
records.keyboard_notes: Resize handle needs a keyboard equivalent if offered.
records.a11y_notes: Reflow must not orphan focus outside the viewport.

records.claim_text: Side panels are barred from detail pages and from multi-column layouts, and must never carry navigation or global finalizing actions.
records.evidence_quote: In the object page floorplan. Use the dynamic side content instead.
records.behaviour_description: Named permitted uses are comments, attachments, pivot table filter and layout, message handling and notifications, and change history. Object data itself always belongs in the content area.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: Contextual side content occupies a default quarter-to-third of screen width, or half in an equal split, and can be placed left or right.
records.evidence_quote: Default split – 25% or 33% of the total screen width
records.behaviour_description: This is the sanctioned side container for detail pages, used for information that enriches or influences the main view such as list filters, chart settings or map details. It is not for splitting a page into two equally important halves and not for drilldown.
records.density_notes: Side content never overlays; the main area narrows to accommodate it.
records.keyboard_notes: Close control lives in the side container's own toolbar.
records.a11y_notes: Reflow below the main content must preserve logical reading order.

records.claim_text: Below 320 pixels of available side width the side content automatically moves beneath the main content, unless configured to hide entirely.
records.evidence_quote: the side content automatically slides under the main content
records.behaviour_description: Because side content may vanish on small screens, nothing critical or uniquely reachable may live there. This is the explicit precondition for using the container at all.
records.density_notes: 320 px is the shared minimum width for both side containers.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Reflowed content must still follow the main content in DOM order.

records.claim_text: Five message types are defined: error blocking progress, warning allowing continuation, success, non-critical information, and confirmation requesting a decision.
records.evidence_quote: An issue has occurred that prevents further processing.
records.behaviour_description: Type selection is driven by consequence, not by tone. The governing principles are to indicate errors and warnings clearly, to weigh carefully how prominent a message needs to be, and to help the user diagnose and resolve rather than merely notifying.
records.density_notes: Semantic colour plus icon; never colour alone.
records.keyboard_notes: Blocking messages must take focus; non-blocking ones must not.
records.a11y_notes: Message type must be conveyed textually as well as by icon and colour.

records.claim_text: Eight message carriers are defined, spanning blocking dialogs, non-blocking collections, transient toasts, inline strips, empty-state illustrations and field-level value states.
records.evidence_quote: SAP Fiori uses the following message controls and visualizations:
records.behaviour_description: Division of labour: a modal box interrupts and demands acknowledgement; a popover collects field-related messages without interrupting; an in-dialog message view collects action-triggered messages not tied to fields; a toast is the default for success; a strip carries page or section level information; an illustration handles empty states; value states handle per-field validation; a small confirmation popover guards cancel.
records.density_notes: Only one strip per area; never stack strips.
records.keyboard_notes: Escape must dismiss non-blocking carriers.
records.a11y_notes: Transient toasts need a live region; they must not be the only channel for important information.

records.claim_text: The message popover collects multiple messages of mixed types in one list, populated automatically at validation points without interrupting the user.
records.evidence_quote: can display multiple messages of different types in one list
records.behaviour_description: Segmented filter buttons at the top narrow the list by type. Each entry carries a short text matching the message shown at the control, plus a subtitle identifying the field or the table row and column, and an optional chevron to a detail view with explanation and resolution guidance.
records.density_notes: Counter property allows aggregating repeated messages into one row.
records.keyboard_notes: Entries navigate focus to the offending field where possible.
records.a11y_notes: When only one message with details exists, the detail view opens directly.

records.claim_text: Messages are grouped by the page section and subsection that produced them, so the list mirrors the page structure.
records.evidence_quote: Messages in the list are grouped by the section and subsection on the UI.
records.behaviour_description: Messages that stem from an action rather than a field are grouped under a last-action heading naming that action, giving a home to messages with no field anchor. Table-originated messages carry the table name alongside the section title.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Group headers should be skippable.
records.a11y_notes: Group headings must be real headings within the popover.

records.claim_text: The footer message button inherits the icon, semantic colour and count of the most critical message type currently in the list, and disappears when there are none.
records.evidence_quote: the message button indicates the most critical message status in the list
records.behaviour_description: One persistent indicator in the footer means validation state is always visible regardless of scroll position, which is the stated reason the pattern exists for long forms.
records.density_notes: It is the one sanctioned exception to the single-emphasised-button rule in a footer.
records.keyboard_notes: Reachable as a normal footer control.
records.a11y_notes: Count and severity must be in the accessible name, not conveyed by colour alone.

records.claim_text: Interruption is reserved for cases genuinely requiring it, typically technical failures; a modal box is used then, otherwise the non-blocking popover.
records.evidence_quote: You need to interrupt the user. In this case, use a message box.
records.behaviour_description: A further exclusion: inside a small dialog the popover would obscure the fields in focus, so inline field highlighting is used instead.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Modal boxes trap and restore focus; popovers must not.
records.a11y_notes: Do not use a modal for information the user can act on later.

records.claim_text: A transient toast is the standard carrier for success confirmation; it self-dismisses and does not interrupt.
records.evidence_quote: The message toast is the standard message component for success messages.
records.behaviour_description: Never confirm success with a modal that requires acknowledgement; the toast keeps the user in flow after a completed save or submit.
records.density_notes: Small, non-disruptive, disappears after a few seconds.
records.keyboard_notes: Must not steal focus.
records.a11y_notes: Requires a polite live region since it vanishes before slow readers reach it.

records.claim_text: For multi-item actions the result pattern is fixed: toast when all succeed, in-dialog message view when none or only some succeed.
records.evidence_quote: When all items were processed successfully, show a message toast.
records.behaviour_description: For partial success the dialog opens with a summary line stating how many of the total were processed, followed by per-item errors and warnings. When some items are known upfront to be ineligible, a warning first asks whether to proceed with the remainder.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Dialog is dismissed by a single close action.
records.a11y_notes: Summary line must be the first item so screen readers get the outcome immediately.

records.claim_text: A bulk action stays enabled if it applies to at least one selected item, is disabled if it applies to none, and selection persists after the action runs.
records.evidence_quote: After the action is applied, keep the items selected.
records.behaviour_description: Per-item state indicators explain why a disabled action is disabled, so the user is not left guessing. Keeping the selection after execution lets the user retry the failed subset without reselecting.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Enablement changes must be perceivable when driven by keyboard selection.
records.a11y_notes: Disabled controls need an accessible explanation of the reason.

records.claim_text: Notifications are transient one-way event messages; engagement is optional, content is immutable once sent, and they may therefore become stale.
records.evidence_quote: Notifications are temporary, one-way messages triggered by an event.
records.behaviour_description: Because content cannot be retracted, notifications must not be the system of record for anything actionable. Grouping similar non-critical event types is recommended once volume rises.
records.density_notes: Panel is a popover anchored to the shell bell control.
records.keyboard_notes: Bell opens the panel; Escape closes and returns focus.
records.a11y_notes: Unread state must be conveyed beyond bold styling.

records.claim_text: The notification panel offers clear-all, sorting by date or importance, and a settings link, over a scrolling list of collapsible groups and items.
records.evidence_quote: Clear All: Removes all notifications
records.behaviour_description: Date is the default sort. Group titles render bold while they contain any unread item. Items carry an optional avatar, a status indicator, title, description, timestamp, an optional importance marker, source information, delete, and a more/less control when text exceeds two lines.
records.density_notes: Title and description each show at most two lines before truncation.
records.keyboard_notes: Group expand/collapse and per-item delete must be focusable.
records.a11y_notes: Status indicator meaning must have a text equivalent.

records.claim_text: Notifications are explicitly distinguished from a message inbox, task centre or feed; those are separate experiences with their own lifecycles.
records.evidence_quote: It is important to distinguish notifications from other similar experiences like a message inbox/mailbox
records.behaviour_description: This is the architectural line for an approval design: the bell announces that an approval arrived, but the queue where approvals are worked is a separate list-style screen with persistence, filtering and bulk actions. Those screens may consume notifications but live in their own context.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: Two density factors exist: a touch-sized one and a reduced one for pointer devices that fits more information per screen.
records.evidence_quote: The compact factor reduces the size of components, so you can display more information
records.behaviour_description: Density is set once for the whole app based on device capability, not per component. Leaving it unset is called out as a defect because different components carry different defaults and the screen ends up mixed.
records.density_notes: Touch density must be applied for touch devices; reduced density for mouse and keyboard.
records.keyboard_notes: Density does not change tab order, only hit-target size.
records.a11y_notes: Reduced density must still meet minimum target size requirements.

records.claim_text: The touch target baseline is 2.75 rem, roughly 44 pixels, shrinking in compact mode where rows and toolbars can drop to about 2 rem.
records.evidence_quote: The default cozy touch area of 2.75 rem (44 px) is reduced in compact mode.
records.behaviour_description: Font size is held constant between densities; only component boxes and the gaps between them shrink. The touchable area is often larger than the visible element, which matters when designing one layout for both input styles.
records.density_notes: Sizing is expressed in root-relative units with a 16 px root, keeping zoom predictable across browsers.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: Holding font size constant protects legibility when density is reduced.

records.claim_text: Phones and tablets are forced to touch density regardless of app declaration or user preference; desktop and hybrid devices honour a user preference where offered.
records.evidence_quote: On phones and tablets, the SAP Fiori launchpad always enforces cozy mode.
records.behaviour_description: Resolution order: device class first, then app-declared support, then user preference. A hybrid device with both input methods falls back to touch density when no preference is stored; a desktop falls back to reduced density.
records.density_notes: A product needing high information density should default to reduced; a spacious product should default to touch.
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: The user preference is itself an accessibility affordance and should not be hidden.

records.claim_text: The tab control serves two distinct purposes: switching between content facets of one object, and acting as a prominent visual filter over a list.
records.evidence_quote: a navigation and filtering control that contains a set of tabs
records.behaviour_description: Filter mode typically opens with an all tab carrying the total count and entity name, followed by per-value tabs with their own counts. It is not for hierarchical navigation and not for jumping to unrelated pages.
records.density_notes: Text-only tabs never truncate, so label length is the constraining factor; icon tabs do truncate.
records.keyboard_notes: Arrow keys move between tabs; the panel is labelled by its tab.
records.a11y_notes: Counters should be part of the tab's accessible name.

records.claim_text: Tabs that do not fit the available width move into an overflow menu; the horizontal arrangement itself never changes.
records.evidence_quote: Overflow menu: Contains any remaining tabs that can’t be displayed in the available space.
records.behaviour_description: Labels are entered in title case with any automatic uppercasing disabled, and counters are rendered inline in parentheses after the label rather than stacked above it.
records.density_notes: Inline counters keep the tab strip to a single row height.
records.keyboard_notes: Overflowed tabs must remain selectable through the overflow control.
records.a11y_notes: Selected tab state must not rely on colour alone.

records.claim_text: Content sits left and actions sit right; navigation affordances live on the left while toolbar actions are right-aligned, keeping the two categories visually distinct.
records.evidence_quote: actions in toolbars are right-aligned
records.behaviour_description: Three toolbar tiers exist: shell level affecting the whole environment, page level affecting the page or its entity, and content level affecting one section such as a table or chart. Actions may also be placed inline in a table row or beside a form field.
records.density_notes: Page-level toolbars are optional and simply absent when no actions exist.
records.keyboard_notes: Tier order in the tab sequence should mirror the visual hierarchy.
records.a11y_notes: Each toolbar needs an accessible name distinguishing its scope.

records.claim_text: Exactly one emphasised primary action is permitted per page, counted across the header and footer toolbars together.
records.evidence_quote: Show only one primary action for the entire page
records.behaviour_description: Header actions are grouped and ordered left to right as business actions, content management, layout management, then generic actions, with importance descending within each group.
records.density_notes: Overflow absorbs low-priority actions first as width shrinks.
records.keyboard_notes: Overflowed actions stay reachable via the overflow control.
records.a11y_notes: Emphasis must not be the only signal of which action is primary.

records.claim_text: Header toolbar actions remain visible at every scroll position and overflow by priority rather than disappearing.
records.evidence_quote: The actions in the header toolbar must always be visible, independent of the scrolling position
records.behaviour_description: Placing entity actions on the title line asserts that the action and the entity sit at the same hierarchy level, which is why they must survive header collapse.
records.density_notes: Sticky behaviour costs a permanent row of vertical space.
records.keyboard_notes: Actions must not be removed from the tab order when the header collapses.
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: The footer floats at the bottom of the screen, never scrolls away, and appears only when there are finalizing actions, message handling or a draft indicator.
records.evidence_quote: The footer toolbar always appears as floating footer at the bottom of the screen.
records.behaviour_description: Reserved strictly for closing and finalizing actions affecting the whole page. Non-finalizing global actions such as edit or delete belong in the header instead, and actions affecting only one container belong beside that container.
records.density_notes: Toolbar height differs between pointer and touch densities.
records.keyboard_notes: Footer is the last tab stop of the page.
records.a11y_notes: Expose as a contentinfo landmark.

records.claim_text: Finalizing actions use text-only right-aligned buttons: emphasised for the primary, ghost for secondary, transparent for negative-path, and semantic for accept or reject.
records.evidence_quote: Use the emphasized button for primary actions, such as Save.
records.behaviour_description: Emphasised and semantic styles must never be mixed in the same toolbar, and only one emphasised button is allowed, with the message indicator as the single documented exception. Icon and text are never combined in one button.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: Labels should be short single-word verbs that survive translation growth.
records.a11y_notes: Semantic colour must be paired with a distinct label.

records.claim_text: Footer buttons are ordered from most to least frequently used so the least important ones overflow first under width pressure.
records.evidence_quote: Buttons are sorted from frequently-used to seldom-used.
records.behaviour_description: Frequency ordering rather than semantic ordering is what makes overflow degradation predictable, since overflow consumes from the trailing end.
records.density_notes: n/a
records.keyboard_notes: n/a
records.a11y_notes: n/a

records.claim_text: All standard components are keyboard-operable by design, with mouse, keyboard and touch treated as equal input channels.
records.evidence_quote: All standard UI elements and controls are designed to be keyboard-enabled.

records.claim_text: A predefined tab order sequence spans the floorplan, the app switch, and navigation within the app, following reading order for the locale.
records.evidence_quote: SAPUI5 supports keyboard navigation with a predefined tab order sequence

records.claim_text: The default theme targets minimum contrast under WCAG 2.2, with additional high-contrast themes reaching a 7:1 text ratio, selectable and persisted per user.
records.evidence_quote: we provide high-contrast themes that support the required contrast ratio of 7:1 for texts

records.claim_text: In display mode object-level messaging uses tags, strips and status text; in edit mode the message popover validates the object's forms and tables as one unit.
records.evidence_quote: use the message popover to help validate forms and tables as a single object
records.behaviour_description: A page-wide strip sits between the title and header content and stays visible when the header collapses; a section-scoped strip sits above its section title. Only one strip per area, never stacked, and the strip must not restate what the status control already says.
records.density_notes: Each strip consumes a full-width row; stacking would push content below the fold.
records.keyboard_notes: Interactive strips need focusable controls.
records.a11y_notes: Strip severity must be announced, not colour-only.

records.claim_text: Side content beside a detail page may hold only contextual material, never object data and never finalizing or global actions.
records.evidence_quote: Do not place object information in the side panel.
records.behaviour_description: The stated reason is spatial: an open side container occupies the full right height of the screen including the header and navigation bands, so it cannot be scoped to sit only under the content area.
records.density_notes: Opening side content narrows the main column across its full height, not just below the header.
records.keyboard_notes: Finalizing actions must remain in the footer where focus expects them.
records.a11y_notes: n/a

gaps: NEGATIVE, WELL DOCUMENTED: no standalone Worklist Floorplan guidelines page exists. Query-index enumeration across every published version (v1-96, v1-108, v1-120, v1-136, v1-139, v1-142, v1-145, v1-148) returns only /discover/frameworks/sap-fiori-elements/list-report/worklist-sap-fiori-elements. Other live pages still hyperlink to a Worklist Floorplan article that is not in the index. All worklist records here are evidenced from that framework article plus the when-to-use-which-floorplan comparison table.

NEGATIVE, WELL DOCUMENTED: no approval-pattern or inbox-floorplan guideline page exists in v1-136. Searched the query-index for approv, inbox, task and workflow. The sanctioned substitutes are the worklist floorplan (bounded queue with predefined views and no filter bar) and global-patterns/messaging/processing-multiple-items (bulk approve/reject enablement and result messaging). The notification article explicitly states an inbox is a DIFFERENT experience from notifications, so an approval inbox must be designed as its own list-style screen, not as a notification surface.

Overview page cards: only the generic card article was transcribed in full. The six concrete card type articles (analytical, list, bar chart list, link list, table, stack/quick view) and the fixed vs resizable card layout articles exist in the index at /page-types/floorplans/overview-page-ovp/cards/** but were not fetched. Fetch these if the design needs per-card-type specifications.

Analytical list page: the article was captured through the content area and view switch. The deeper subsections (KPI tag and KPI card specifications, visual filter chart types, drilldown and slice-and-dice interaction detail) were beyond the transcription window.

Keyboard interaction specifics are thin across the whole guideline set. The object page article references an internal Fiori Keyboard Interaction document that is marked internal-only and is not published. Only fragments (arrow keys between anchors, initial focus rules per floorplan) are publicly evidenced. Do not assume a fuller public keyboard spec exists.

Theming and design tokens were deliberately NOT transcribed. Rule 7 forbids capturing theme hex values, so no colour, spacing token, or typography scale values are recorded. The design system must derive its own token values; only the structural rule (tokens feed themes feed components) is captured.

help.sap.com and learning.sap.com were not needed for this lane. www.sap.com/design-system rendered fully through the in-app browser, so every record here is Tier 1 first-party primary guidance rather than Tier 2 course material. 1dsag.github.io was not consulted and is not cited.

Version pinning risk: all records cite v1-136. The index shows v1-148 as the newest and v1-139 to v1-148 also live. Slugs were verified for v1-136 only. If a downstream gate re-fetches, use v1-136 URLs verbatim or re-verify slugs, since the site has already deprecated at least one floorplan slug (list-report deprecated at 1.71).
